title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: This is the title page and opening paragraph of E526, 'Investigatio motuum quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt' (Acta Academiae Scientiarum Petropolitanae, 1779 volume, printed 1782, p. 103 ff.). There is no mathematics on the page yet; it is a programmatic introduction. In modern terms Euler says: (1) the transverse vibration of elastic laminae and rods was treated long ago, at length, by Daniel Bernoulli and by himself. (2) At that time two things were not yet mature: the mechanical principles from which such motions must be derived, and the part of analysis dealing with functions of two variables, i.e. partial differential equations in x and t. So redoing the problem is not 'actum agere' (doing what is already done). (3) Many different kinds of motion can occur in such bodies and need a more exact analysis. He will derive the whole theory from first principles, more clearly than before, and set out all possible kinds of motion; in modern terms these are the different end conditions and modes. (4) To this end he states two lemmas: one for the equilibrium of a rod of arbitrary (variable) elasticity under arbitrary distributed forces, and one for its motion. The next page shows that both rod and forces are assumed to lie in one plane. The proofs are omitted because Euler says he has given them elsewhere, including a version for non-planar motion. The equilibrium lemma on the next page is the bending-moment balance: the moment of the applied loads, ∫dy∫P ds − ∫dx∫Q ds, equals V/r, the elastic moment, i.e. stiffness divided by radius of curvature (the Bernoulli–Euler law). This introduction serves to set up the linearized beam equation with its eigenfunctions and the frequency equations for the various boundary conditions.

ideas.what: Historical remark that the rod-vibration problem had been treated earlier by Daniel Bernoulli and by Euler, but before the general dynamical principles and PDE theory were developed
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam vibration; historiography of the beam equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler, c. 1735–1744 (Euler's treatment in the elastica appendix of the Methodus inveniendi, E65, 1744)
ideas.where_published: E65 (Additamentum I, De curvis elasticis, 1744). The episode is discussed in Truesdell, 'The Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788' (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Plan to derive the equations of equilibrium and motion of a rod of variable elasticity under arbitrary forces as two lemmas, with proofs given 'alio loco', including the non-planar case
ideas.modern_name: Balance of forces and moments for a rod (Kirchhoff-type rod equations, planar case)
ideas.where_published: Euler's late papers on the equilibrium and motion of flexible and elastic bodies, e.g. E481 'De gemina methodo tam aequilibrium quam motum corporum flexibilium determinandi' (exact cross-reference unsure); covered in Truesdell

deep.surprise_reason: This is an introductory paragraph whose content (a revisit of the beam vibration problem with mature principles and PDE methods) is well documented in Truesdell's history and the Opera omnia commentary. There is no new mathematical content on this page.
